description: The cores one hosted cluster of each t-shirt size takes on a full management cluster, written by hack/hcp-scale-analysis/cores_per_cluster.py from size-pods.json. The settings are placeholders to confirm.

fields.basis: reserved: packs what the pods reserve today; used: what they use
fields.full_machines_per_zone: control-plane machines in each zone of a full management cluster
fields.other_machines: the machines a management cluster runs besides its control-plane machines
fields.limit: the most hosted clusters on one management cluster
fields.new_management_cluster_cores: the cores of a full management cluster, control-plane and other machines: quota is planned per management cluster, for all its machines at their largest, so a region that needs another one needs all of these at once
fields.clusters_that_fit: the most clusters of the size that fit on a management cluster with 1, 2, ... control-plane machines per zone, by the rules pack_clusters.py follows
fields.not_proven: for numbers of machines per zone where clusters_that_fit isn't proven to be the most possible: the most the machines' room allows in total
fields.clusters: how many clusters of the size a full management cluster holds: those that fit, at most the limit
fields.runs_out_of: the resource clusters of the size run out of first on a full management cluster
fields.limited_by: what stops more clusters of the size going on a full management cluster: runs_out_of, or the limit
fields.own_cores: one cluster's own share of a full management cluster's control-plane machines: their cores over the clusters that fit
fields.shared_cores: one cluster's share of what's there for all the clusters: the machines a management cluster runs besides its control-plane machines, and any control-plane room the limit leaves unused
fields.cores: own_cores and shared_cores added up: a full management cluster's cores over the clusters it holds
